chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Charity (sadaqa) repels the evil death.'

key_terms.الصَّدَقَة: Sadaqa — voluntary charity beyond obligatory zakat; a broad term for any act of giving for God's sake
key_terms.مِيتَة السَّوْء: Evil death — dying in a bad or wretched manner, without repentance or in a state of sin

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about charity and protection from evil death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates a saying of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) that giving sadaqa (voluntary charity) has the spiritual power to ward off a bad or evil death. This hadith appears in the first chapter of Kitab al-Zakat in Al-Kafi, which is devoted to the merits and virtues of charity. The concept of 'evil death' (mitat al-saw') refers to dying in a state of sin, disgrace, or sudden violent death without the chance for repentance — a feared outcome in early Islamic piety circles.
